paper.title: Generalized Risk-Aversion in Stochastic Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Risk-averse stochastic bandit with continuous risk function f(mean, variance)
unmapped: Best arm and regret defined by a risk measure f(mu_i, sigma_i^2) of mean and variance (minimised), not by the mean
The learner knows the function f and a modulus of continuity phi for it
settings.definition_quote: the learner is supplied by a function $f: D \ra \nR$, where $D = \left[0,1\right]\times \left[0, 1 \right]$ ... $\regret_n = \sum_{t=1}^{n}f_{a_t} - n \cdot f_{i^\star}$

settings.name_in_paper: Risk-averse stochastic bandit with discontinuous risk function satisfying Assumption 1
unmapped: Best arm and regret defined by a risk measure f(mu_i, sigma_i^2) of mean and variance (minimised), not by the mean
The learner knows f, its discontinuity set (distance d_Omega), and local moduli of continuity phi_i (paper notes knowledge of e_i could be avoided)
Assumption 1: f is continuous in a neighbourhood of each arm's (mean, variance) point
settings.definition_quote: For each arm $i$ there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $f$ is continuous in $B_i(\varepsilon) = \left\lbrace (x,y) \in D : d_i(x,y) \leq \varepsilon \right\rbrace $.

symbols.phi_inv: inverse of the strictly increasing modulus of continuity phi of f (Lemma 1)

conditions: risk-averse regret sum_t f_{a_t} - n f_{i*} with f_i = f(mu_i, sigma_i^2)

source.label: theorem:continuous
source.quote: Consider a continuous function $f$, then for $\delta\in(0,\frac{1}{4Kn})$ with probability at least $1-4Kn\delta$ the regret of the $\varphi$-LCB algorithm at time $n$ is upper bounded by: \[ \regret_n \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{18\cdot \Delta_i \cdot \ln\frac{1}{\delta}}{(\invphi(\Delta_i/2))^2} + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \Delta_i\enspace , \]

results.notes: Regret is a pseudo-regret on the risk measure f; recorded as quantity 'other' per risk-aware guidance.

symbols.phi_inv: inverse of the modulus of continuity phi of f

source.label: theorem:continuous
source.quote: Moreover, for $n > 4K$, if the algorithm is run with $\delta = \frac{1}{n^2}$, then with probability at least $1-\frac{4K}{n}$ the regret is upper bounded by: \[ \regret_n \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{36\cdot \Delta_i}{(\invphi(\Delta_i/2))^2}\ln{n} + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \Delta_i\enspace . \]

results.notes: Paper also gives a non-Hölder example h(x) with bound sum 9 Delta_i e^{4/Delta_i} ln n + sum Delta_i (not recorded separately).

conditions: f is L-Lipschitz (w.r.t. l1 norm on (mean, variance))

source.label: theorem:continuous
source.quote: when $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz, i.e. $\varphi(z) = Lz$, the regret bound is \[ \regret_n \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{144\cdot L^2}{\Delta_i}\ln{n} + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \Delta_i \]

results.notes: Specialization stated in the 'Efficiency' discussion following Theorem 1, not a numbered statement.

conditions: f is alpha-Hölder with constant L

source.label: theorem:continuous
source.quote: when $f$ is $\alpha$-H\"{o}lder continuous, i.e. $\varphi(z) = Lz^\alpha$, the regret bound is \[ \regret_n \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{36\cdot (2\cdot L)^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}}{(\Delta_i)^{\frac{2-\alpha}{\alpha}}}\ln{n} + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \Delta_i\enspace . \]

results.notes: Specialization from the Efficiency discussion; L_lip here is the Hölder constant.

symbols.e_i: l1 distance from (mu_i, sigma_i^2) to the closest discontinuity of f
symbols.phi_i_inv: inverse of the local modulus of continuity phi_i of f around arm i

conditions: Assumption 1: f continuous in a neighbourhood of each arm's (mean, variance)

source.label: theorem:discontinuous
source.quote: Consider function $f$ that satisfies Assumption \ref{assumption1}. Then for $\delta\in (0,\frac{1}{4Kn})$ with probability at least $1-4Kn\delta$ for all $n \geq \sum_{i=1..K} 162\cdot e_i^{-2}\ln\frac{1}{\delta}$ the regret of the $\varphi$-LCB2 algorithm at time $n$ is upper bounded by: \[ \regret_n \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0}\Delta_i\left( 162e_i^{-2} + \frac{18}{(\invphi_i(\Delta_i/2))^2} \right) \ln\frac{1}{\delta} + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0}\Delta_i \]

results.notes: Compute depends on evaluating d_Omega; constant time for threshold variance.

symbols.e_i: l1 distance from (mu_i, sigma_i^2) to the closest discontinuity of f
symbols.phi_i_inv: inverse of the local modulus of continuity phi_i

source.label: theorem:discontinuous
source.quote: Moreover, if the algorithm is run with $\delta = \frac{1}{n^2}$, then with probability at least $1-\frac{4K}{n}$ for all $n \geq \sum_{i=1..K} 324\cdot e_i^{-2}\ln n$ the regret is upper bounded by: \[ \regret_n \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0}\Delta_i\left( 324e_i^{-2} + \frac{36}{(\invphi_i(\Delta_i/2))^2} \right) \ln{n} + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0}\Delta_i\enspace . \]

results.notes: Threshold-variance specialization: sum 4(81 e_i^{-2} Delta_i + 36/Delta_i) ln n + sum Delta_i (not recorded separately).
